ops.body:
Warm-start findings from the 2026-07-11 follow-ups recon (task deliberately left in backlog by user decision that round):

- Today mcp__cc-context__ccx_code_edit / ccx_code_replace parse via parse_tool_call to the generic MCP path; the ccx MCP edit aliases already agree with file_path_of (the alias mapping exists), so file-path attribution works — what's missing is lowering the inputs to a typed edit call.
- Shape mismatch blocks a naive lowering to EditCall: ccx_code_edit takes an anchored range (--at A-B#hash) + content / --delete, not old_string/new_string. The likely design is an McpEditCall-ish type with parse_tool_call wiring plus its own file_path_of/hunks_of arms, NOT reuse of EditCall.
- Cross-repo dependency unconfirmed: captain-hook hooks consume the typed tool layer; which consumers would key on the new type (vs today's generic McpCall) needs confirming before the shape is fixed.
- Rust parity: a new typed call in cc_transcript/tools.py lands with its Rust mirror in the same commit per AGENTS.md "Rust parity is atomic" — budget for the port when scoping.
